# Review Entry - One Local Diff, Then Stop

Use the existing `/atom:review` skill and `atom review` command. This reference
defines their bounded entry contract, not a new command or runtime approval
mechanism. Instructions do not prove that a live agent waits or respects refusal.

## Select The Mode

An explicit review-only request is **standalone**, even if `.atom/` exists.
No initialization, registered phase, POC or design spec is required for reviewing
an existing diff. Do not run `atom status`, search for phase artifacts or adopt
the lifecycle just to perform this review.

Use **phase review** when the current developer-approved work explicitly calls
for it. Retain the established phase report, project audit artifacts and gate.
The presence of Atom files alone does not choose this mode. If intent is truly
ambiguous, ask one focused question rather than inventing project context.

## Inspect Without Starting Review

Establish the local Git target and the intended changes through read-only
inspection. Choose exactly one source: unstaged working changes (`--working`),
staged changes (`--staged`), or committed branch changes against an explicit
reference (`--branch REF`). Do not assume the reference is main or include
untracked files that Git's selected diff does not contain.

If command forms are unknown, use [bootstrap.md](bootstrap.md) and supported
help checks. No separate Atom checkout or inspection of installed Python source
is needed. Missing commands require an installation proposal and consent, not
automatic installation or PATH changes.

Read the root module/configuration only as needed for the selected review.
Missing root `go.mod` does not require `atom init`: disclose that Go tooling will
be skipped. Offer setup separately only if the developer wants it; review intent
is not permission to create a module or repair source.

## Propose Before Probes Or Paid Work

Present one concrete plan, then ask for approval and stop:

- Target directory and exact diff selector/reference.
- Actual reviewer model identifiers, number of runs, concurrency and expected
  submission count. Include availability probes in the call budget: two models
  with one run each can involve two probes plus two review submissions. Do not
  promise a token or monetary ceiling the runtime does not enforce.
- Normal Go checks, missing/skipped evidence and relevant side effects. Go checks
  may invoke project build commands, dependencies, toolchains and caches; ordinary
  review is not inherently offline, read-only or free of cache writes.
- Report format and exact report/audit paths, including any directories created.
- The review-only exit: report and triage, not fixes, setup, phase advancement,
  commit, push or publication.

Recommend one run per model and concurrency 1 as a bounded starting choice,
not a change to CLI defaults. Choose at least two different reviewer models,
neither the authoring model. Resolve unknown identities/authorship explicitly;
do not infer independence from a label. This is skill policy, not CLI enforcement.

Use actual approved identifiers rather than silently accepting CLI defaults.
Repeated `--model NAME` selects reviewers; without it the CLI has built-in
defaults. It does **not** resolve reviewer model roles from `.atom/config.json`.
That file may independently configure Go-version policy. General role advice in
[model-guidance.md](model-guidance.md) does not change this CLI-specific contract.

No reviewer availability probe or review submission occurs before approval.
Earlier setup/phase approval is not automatically approval of this review spend.
If declined, do not launch reviewers, create the bundle or modify the target.
A changed selector, additional runs/models, installation, gate bypass, fix or
publication requires a separately approved scope. Never silently retry a failed
review with more spend or a different toolchain.

## Execute Only The Approved Command

These are alternatives, not a batch to run. Replace MODEL_A and MODEL_B with
approved available identifiers and use the approved branch reference:

```text
atom review --working --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
atom review --staged --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
atom review --branch main --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
```

Add `--json` only when that output was selected. Use the successful command form
from bootstrap. Keep normal gates enabled; do not add `--skip-toolchain`, change
Go versions or repair the diff to get past a failure. Existing explicit advanced
options remain available under their own approved scope, not as automatic recovery.

Formatting checks selected surviving changed Go snapshots without rewriting them.
Build, vet, test and race checks instead examine the working module, not an
isolated staged index or committed branch tree. Passed race tests cover exercised
paths only. Absent optional analyzers and missing-module tooling exclude nothing.

Surface actual required-gate failures and stop this bounded action. An exit-0
report with missing `go.mod` is still unverified tooling evidence, not a verified
build or application. Distinguish skipped checks, unavailable/silent/unparsed
responses, partial participation and genuinely empty findings. No usable response
is not a clean review. If fewer than two qualifying independent models answered,
report that the skill's multi-model obligation remains unmet; do not invent
participation or automatically retry.

## Persist And Triage Without Adopting A Lifecycle

The CLI emits its report to stdout; it does not choose a phase path. The skill
proposes a small standalone bundle, for example:

```text
specs/reviews/<slug>/review.md
specs/reviews/<slug>/findings.md
specs/reviews/<slug>/decisions.md
```

Choose the exact permitted paths with the developer before creating anything.
For phase review, retain `specs/{project}/phase-NN-{slug}/review.md` and the
project's existing findings/decisions locations instead.

Preserve the actual runtime report and participation/evidence limitations.
Always produce `findings.md` and `decisions.md`, even when they say "No findings."
and "No deviations." Use `atom-write-artifact` for these `specs/**` artifacts,
obtaining its repository-scoped permission on first use. Check existing paths;
do not overwrite conflicting work. Any writer refusal or nonzero exit is a
blocker: surface it and stop, without a generic editor or alternate path.

If the developer declines audit-file creation, explain that the skill cannot
complete its persisted audit under this plan. Do not silently drop the records
or force a phase directory. Direct CLI stdout behavior remains available and
unchanged; that is not permission to execute a different paid plan.

Triage high-consequence findings with the developer. Record deferrals/rejections
and reasons. Any fix is a separate approved action with appropriate verification,
not part of review-only consent.

**Standalone stops here:** present report, triage and remaining limitations.
Do not invoke ship, start another phase or modify source automatically.
**Phase review** presents its normal gate and may recommend its next beat; that
recommendation does not authorize executing it.

---
name: review
description: 'Standalone or phase multi-model review of a Go diff, merged into one report with severities. Keywords: review, code review, multi-model review, review my changes, review the diff, critique.'
---

# /atom:review

Reviews a diff with **two or more different models** and merges their findings into one
report.

## Why more than one model

A model reviewing its own output shares its own blind spots. It will not flag the
misunderstanding that produced the code, because it still holds that
misunderstanding.

> **The reviewing model must not be the model that wrote the code.**

This is the entire point of the skill. A single-model self-review is not a substitute,
and running one instead is the rationalization this skill exists to prevent.

## When to use

- For a bounded standalone review, without Atom initialization or phase state
- After `/atom:tdd` for a phase
- Before `/atom:ship`
- Any time a diff is large enough that reading it once isn't enough

## Writing artifacts

Send complete review reports, findings, and decisions as UTF-8 standard input to
`atom-write-artifact <relative-path>`. Treat any refusal or non-zero exit as a blocker;
never bypass it with a generic editor or another shell command.

## Step 0 — Scope, propose and wait

Read [standalone-review.md](../atom/references/standalone-review.md) first.
Follow its mode, prerequisite, consent, model-budget and artifact contract in
both standalone and phase contexts. Explicit review-only intent remains standalone
even in an initialized project. Do not require phase discovery or onboarding.

Propose the exact target/diff, actual models, runs/concurrency, evidence and file
effects before availability probes or review submissions. Wait for approval;
refusal launches no reviewers and creates no bundle. Do not call `atom review`
merely to discover the diff or probe models before that gate.

## Step 1 — Establish the diff without calling reviewers

```bash
git diff main...HEAD             # inspect committed changes against agreed main
git diff --staged                # inspect staged changes
git diff                         # inspect unstaged working changes
```

Choose only the intended source/reference; main above is an example, not a default.
Inspect surrounding code as needed for triage. The CLI supplies the selected diff
and its evidence, not an automatic whole-file context or approved design spec.
Do not claim reviewers received context that was not actually supplied.

## Step 2 — Let the toolchain answer first

No separate command: the gate runs inside `atom review`, before the models.

For a normal review with a root Go module, Atom runs `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `go test`
and `go test -race`, plus `staticcheck`, `errcheck` and `govulncheck` when they are
installed.

Review formatting checks whole surviving changed Go files from the selected
working-tree, staged or committed-branch snapshot, using stdin without rewriting
source. Untouched files are not scanned. The report names checked paths and
outside-module or nested-module exclusions; zero applicable files means SKIPPED,
not a formatting pass. Other review checks retain their existing module-wide
scope, and standalone `atom check` retains module-wide formatting.
Those module-wide checks run against the working tree, not an isolated staged
or committed tree. Without root `go.mod`, tooling is explicitly skipped: an exit-0
report does not verify a build. Missing optional tools exclude nothing.

**A failing required gate stops the review.** Reviewing code that does not compile, or
that `go vet` already objects to, spends model attention on a question that has an
exact free answer — and the findings would be about code you are about to change
anyway.

What passed is then written into the prompt as **excluded**: the models are told not to
re-report an ignored error, a vet diagnostic, a formatting complaint, or a data race on
a tested path. That exclusion is the mechanism that frees attention for the rest of this
page.

These rules keep the exclusion honest:

- **A tool that did not run excludes nothing.** If `errcheck` is not installed, the
  prompt says so and ignored errors stay in scope. Suppressing a category nobody checked
  is how real bugs go missing.
- **Clean is not absent.** `go test -race` only observes paths the tests actually
  executed. Concurrent code with no test is unchecked, not safe — and the prompt says
  that in those words.
- **Formatting proof is file-scoped.** Only the checked snapshots are excluded
  from formatting review; excluded modules and a skipped formatter are not clean.

`--skip-toolchain` bypasses the gate. The prompt then tells the models that nothing was
checked and nothing is excluded, so a skipped gate costs attention rather than silently
hiding findings.
Do not select this bypass or another Go version as automatic failure recovery;
the shared entry contract requires approval of changed evidence/scope.

### Optional exact Go selection

The launch module's existing `.atom/config.json` may set `review_go_version` to an
exact stable `1.X.Y` patch (X >= 21). `--go-version 1.X.Y` overrides it for one run;
`--go-executable PATH` selects an already installed direct `bin/go` (Windows:
`bin/go.exe`) and requires an effective version. No installation, automatic upgrade,
ancestor lookup or version inference from `go.mod` occurs. Malformed present config
is an explicit error. Explicit paths resolve from launch cwd before PR preparation;
target checkout policy never replaces the frozen launch request.

Bounded installed-location discovery may need an explicit path for custom layouts.
Selected direct Go gates and selected-root gofmt retain existing gate semantics;
pinned Makefile build/test delegation fails before probes or recipes rather than
bypassing the project's build. Unpinned delegation is unchanged. Advisory helper-Go
settings are selected, not analyzer binaries/compiler internals or model tools.
Child-only settings do not change defaults or make dependency activity network-free.

Reports/prompts distinguish requested from observed versions. Configured pins with
`--skip-toolchain`, or requests outside a root Go module, remain `not_run` with no
observed executable/probes. Explicit Go flags plus `--skip-toolchain` are usage
errors. Missing, mismatched or changed executable identities and required failures
still block review; no compiler-text-based continuation is permitted.

## Step 3 — Run the models

```bash
atom review --branch main --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
```

Run only the complete approved command. MODEL_A and MODEL_B are placeholders for
actual approved available models, neither the author. Use the agreed selector;
working/staged alternatives are in the shared reference. Runs=1/concurrency=1 is
a bounded recommendation, not the CLI default.

Each model run receives the full selected diff and evidence, not a separate
invocation for each file. Runs do not receive each other's findings; concurrency
is controlled by the approved option. The CLI uses repeated `--model` values or
built-in defaults, not general model-role resolution from `.atom/config.json`.
Report unavailable, silent, unparsed or insufficient independent responses
honestly; do not substitute a clean review or automatically retry.

## Step 4 — What reviewers look for

Only successful, applicable toolchain evidence is excluded. Unchecked concerns remain
in scope. What is left is
the set of questions no tool can answer — and it is deliberately short, because a
reviewer handed thirty concerns reports on none of them well.

| Priority | Category | Why no tool catches it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Wrong logic** | It compiles, vets clean and the tests pass — because the tests assert the wrong thing |
| 2 | **Untested concurrency** | The race detector only observes paths the tests ran. A goroutine with no test is unchecked |
| 3 | **Misleading names** | A name that says the wrong thing costs every future reader, and no linter can tell |
| 4 | **Code that resists extension** | A wide interface or a package-level dependency forces the next change to edit working code |
| 5 | **Contract drift** | The code disagrees with the approved design spec, which no tool has read |
| 6 | **Tests that cannot fail** | A green suite that asserts nothing looks identical to a green suite that works |
| 7 | **Unvalidated input** | `govulncheck` finds known holes in dependencies, never the one you just wrote |

Severity still comes from consequence. A finding that cannot be stated as "this breaks
when X" is a preference, and preferences are the findings reviewers drop first. That is
measured, not assumed: seeded defects phrased as style preferences were reported by
nobody, while defects with a visible consequence were reported by everybody — even when
the reviewer was handed the exact rule.

[go-style.md](../atom/references/go-style.md) is the reference behind priorities 3 and 4.
Use it to explain a finding, not as a checklist to walk: thirty rules handed to a
reviewer produce worse coverage than seven.

Formatting in the checked file snapshots is **not** reviewed. `gofmt` settled it
for those files only; a skipped formatter or an excluded module proves nothing
about formatting there.

> **Where the real instruction lives.** This table guides *your* triage. The sentences
> actually sent to the models are `REVIEW_PROMPT` and the toolchain block in
> `tools/atom/review.py`. Changing this table alone changes nothing the models see —
> if you want different findings, change the prompt and re-measure.

## Step 5 — Capture the actual merged report

The runtime groups findings by file and line proximity, retaining every message
and severity disagreement. This is not semantic deduplication: nearby reports
may describe different defects. It emits Markdown or JSON to stdout.

Persist the report at the approved mode-specific path from the shared reference.
Standalone uses its small review/findings/decisions bundle; phase review retains
`specs/{project}/phase-NN-{slug}/review.md` and existing project audit locations.

Each merged finding carries:

- **Severity** — critical / high / medium / low, with disagreements retained
- **Agreement** — participating models and per-model reporting runs
- **Location** — `file:line`
- **Messages** — the original findings; a concrete suggested fix is not guaranteed

**Agreement is a signal, not a verdict.** Read critical/high findings individually,
including single-model findings. Group proximity or identical synthetic replies
are not proof of independent corroboration or correctness.

## Step 6 — Triage with the developer

Go through critical/high findings together. For each: propose a separately
approved fix, defer to `findings.md` with a reason, or reject with a reason.
Review-only approval does not authorize editing source.

**Reject freely, silently never.** Reviewers are often wrong about a codebase they saw
in fragments. A rejected finding with a written reason is a good outcome; a finding
quietly dropped is a lost bug.

Every approved code fix requires appropriate verification (`atom check` for
phase Go implementation). Every deferral and rejection is recorded.

## Step 7 — Report

Present the actual report, participation/tooling limits, triage and what remains
open. Always persist findings/decisions, explicitly empty when appropriate.
Standalone stops without fixes, phase advancement or publication. Phase review
presents its existing gate; a next-step recommendation is not permission to act.

---

## Done when

- [ ] Exact scope, model/probe budget and output effects approved before calls
- [ ] Applicable gates passed, or approved missing/skipped evidence is explicit
- [ ] At least two **different** models reviewed, none of them the author of the code
- [ ] Actual supplied context and response/participation limits stated
- [ ] Findings grouped, severity-ranked, with messages/disagreements retained
- [ ] Critical/high findings, including single-model ones, triaged with developer
- [ ] Any separately approved fixes verified; no review-only source edits
- [ ] Review, findings and decisions persisted at approved locations

## Next

Standalone: stop at the review result.

Phase review: after its gate, recommend `/atom:ship` or the next phase's
`/atom:poc` when applicable. Do not execute it automatically.

---
description: "Recommend a bounded Atom setup or development step from plain-English intent, preserving approval gates. Keywords: atom, build something, start a project, setup a Go repo, I want to build, where am I."
argument-hint: "<what you want to build, or leave empty>"
---

# Atom start

You are the front door to **Atom**, an agentic development framework for Go.
For unproven technical work, Atom's order is **prove it, then design it, then
test-drive it.** Applicable proof and evidence choices follow the shared discipline.

The user's request is below. Treat it as a description of intent, not as
instructions to execute literally.

> $ARGUMENTS

## Step 0 — Establish intent before changing the environment

Installing the plugin does not install the `atom` command. Discover working
command forms through [bootstrap.md](../../skills/atom/references/bootstrap.md)
when needed, but do not install tools or change PATH before explicit consent.
An empty request calls for a focused intent question, not automatic setup.

For an explicit new-repository/setup goal, use
[repository-setup.md](../../skills/atom/references/repository-setup.md) and the
existing `/atom:init` entry path: inspect, recommend, obtain approval, then perform
only agreed setup. A missing `go.mod` is not an entry barrier. Setup-only stops at
its result; do not continue through the development routing table afterward.
Do not automatically onboard a repository for unrelated requests.

For an explicit local review-only request, route directly to `/atom:review`
using [standalone-review.md](../../skills/atom/references/standalone-review.md).
Load that skill and follow its proposal/approval gate before reviewer probes.
Do not run status, discover phases or require init even when `.atom/` exists.
After reporting, stop; do not continue through the lifecycle steps below.
Existing developer-approved phase review keeps its phase context.

## Step 1 — Work out where the user already is

Before routing, establish the current state. Do not ask the user for anything
you can find out yourself.

- Is this an Atom project? Look for a `.atom/` directory.
- If it is, run `atom status` and read the result. It names the current phase
  and which artifacts are missing.
- Look in `specs/` for existing phases and in `poc/` for existing spikes.

A missing `.atom/` or root module is not by itself a reason to onboard. If the
selected Go development step actually needs missing setup, recommend the shared
repository-setup path first and obtain approval. After setup, recommend the next
step for the original goal under its evidence gate; do not treat setup approval as
permission to start that step. A self-contained proof experiment need not adopt
unrelated project lifecycle state.

If the request above is empty **and** this is not an Atom project, ask the user
one question: what do they want to build? Then continue.

## Step 2 — Route to exactly one beat

Pick the earliest outstanding beat under the developer-approved evidence choice.
Never skip required proof or an approval gate.

First assess intent, uncertainty and applicable evidence using
[poc-discipline.md](../../skills/atom/references/poc-discipline.md). Explain one
recommended next evidence step and its alternative; let the developer decide at
the applicable gate. The table is the full path for unproven technical work, not
a reason to manufacture a POC for an understood regression, proven wiring, or
documentation. Reused/regression proof needs its recorded justification and
approval; production work still requires an approved spec and TDD. This guidance
adds no command or automatic routing and does not alter runtime phase checks.

| Situation | Route to | Slash command |
|---|---|---|
| Explicit Go repository setup, including missing module | Approved bounded setup, then stop if setup-only | `/atom:init` |
| Intent or acceptance is missing | Scope the work by interview | `/atom:discover` |
| Material technical uncertainty remains without applicable proof | Scope and run the throwaway spike | `/atom:poc` |
| Confirmed POC approved, or applicable regression/prior evidence approved and recorded | Write the design spec from that evidence | `/atom:spec` |
| No material technical uncertainty; specifically justified POC skip explicitly approved and recorded | Write the design spec, stating assumptions and evidence limits | `/atom:spec` |
| Spec agreed | Derive tests and red-green for runtime code, or factual/documentation checks for documentation-only work | `/atom:tdd` |
| Code exists, needs a second opinion | Multi-model review | `/atom:review` |
| Work is ready to land | Commit, branch, PR | `/atom:ship` |
| Too big for one pass | Break into phases | `/atom:plan` |

If a regression, evidence-reuse, or no-uncertainty route is proposed but not yet
approved, present the evidence-choice recommendation under the shared discipline
and stop at its gate before routing onward. For an approved regression route,
capture the failing test as defect proof before drafting the spec if that proof
does not already exist; do not implement the fix before spec approval.
Documentation-only work uses factual review and relevant checks under the
repository's review/approval expectations, not an invented Go spike.

Announce the beat you picked and **why**, in one line, then carry out that
skill's workflow. Load the skill rather than improvising its steps.

## Step 3 — Scope the POC before building it

If a new POC is needed and you routed to `/atom:discover` or `/atom:poc`, the goal
of the conversation is a **single falsifiable question** — one the spike can
answer with evidence, not an opinion.

Interview the user **one question at a time**. Good questions to draw on:

- What part of this are you least sure will actually work?
- What would have to be true for this to be worth building?
- What would convince you this approach is wrong?
- What is the smallest thing that would settle that?

Do not accept a vague goal such as "make it fast". Push until the question has
an observable outcome and a threshold agreed *before* the spike runs.

State the question back to the user and get agreement before writing code.

## Step 4 — State the outcome or the bounded next recommendation

For ongoing development, name one appropriate next command and its purpose as a
recommendation, not permission to execute it. At an approval gate, present the
artifact and decision needed, then wait. For example:

    Next: /atom:spec — turn the POC's verdict into a design spec.

For completed setup-only work, report the result and limitations, then stop.
Do not manufacture another command or treat CLI-printed POC advice as approval.

## Conventions that always apply

- Go code favours **readability and extensibility over idiomatic terseness**,
  with meaningful comments explaining intent.
- A POC is **disposable**. It answers one question and is not production code.
- Thresholds are **pre-registered** before a spike runs, and are not moved
  afterwards to rescue a result. If an instrument was wrong, fix the
  instrument and say so.

For one local diff, use `/atom:review` directly. An explicit review-only request
routes there before status/phase discovery, even if `.atom/` exists. You do not
need onboarding, a registered phase or a root `go.mod`. The
[shared review-entry contract](../skills/atom/references/standalone-review.md)
defines the bounded action.

The skill inspects the target read-only and proposes the exact working, staged
or branch source, concrete independent models, runs/concurrency, availability
probes and review submissions, normal checks and output effects. It waits for
approval before reviewer calls. Declining creates no report bundle or setup;
revised scope requires a new decision. Ordinary Go checks may use dependencies,
project build commands and caches; review is not inherently offline.

The CLI's actual options are `--working`, `--staged`, `--branch REF` and repeated
`--model NAME`. Models come from those flags or built-in defaults, not general
role resolution from `.atom/config.json`. Explicit Go-version policy is separate.
The CLI emits Markdown or `--json` to stdout; the skill proposes a small approved
`specs/reviews/<slug>/` bundle containing review, findings and decisions rather
than creating lifecycle state. Audit-file refusal is surfaced, not silently waived.

Required-gate failures stop the bounded action. Without root `go.mod`, tooling
is explicitly skipped; a completed report is not a verified application.
Formatting checks selected changed snapshots, but module-wide build/vet/test/race
check the working tree. Unavailable or silent reviewers are not clean results.
The result names actual participation and missing evidence.

Standalone stops after reporting and triage, without source fixes, phase
advancement or shipping. Phase review within existing approved work retains its
phase report, audit locations and gate. Instructions and documentation checks
do not establish that a live model will wait, honor refusal or stop.

"""Check shipped review entry contracts without launching reviewer processes."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
import re
import shlex
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

import pytest

from atom.cli import _build_parser


REPOSITORY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
REFERENCE = Path("skills") / "atom" / "references" / "standalone-review.md"
REVIEW_SKILL = Path("skills") / "review" / "SKILL.md"
ASSETS = Path("tools") / "atom" / "assets"
DOCUMENTS = (
    REFERENCE,
    REVIEW_SKILL,
    ASSETS / REFERENCE,
    ASSETS / REVIEW_SKILL,
    Path("com.github.copilot") / "commands" / "start.md",
    Path("README.md"),
    Path("docs") / "workflow.md",
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("relative", (REFERENCE, REVIEW_SKILL))
def test_review_entry_assets_match_canonical_bytes(relative: Path) -> None:
    canonical = REPOSITORY / relative
    assert canonical.is_file(), f"Missing canonical entry guidance: {relative}"
    assert (REPOSITORY / ASSETS / relative).read_bytes() == canonical.read_bytes()


def test_start_routes_review_before_lifecycle_inspection() -> None:
    start = (REPOSITORY / "com.github.copilot" / "commands" / "start.md").read_text(

# Review Entry - One Local Diff, Then Stop

Use the existing `/atom:review` skill and `atom review` command. This reference
defines their bounded entry contract, not a new command or runtime approval
mechanism. Instructions do not prove that a live agent waits or respects refusal.

## Select The Mode

An explicit review-only request is **standalone**, even if `.atom/` exists.
No initialization, registered phase, POC or design spec is required for reviewing
an existing diff. Do not run `atom status`, search for phase artifacts or adopt
the lifecycle just to perform this review.

Use **phase review** when the current developer-approved work explicitly calls
for it. Retain the established phase report, project audit artifacts and gate.
The presence of Atom files alone does not choose this mode. If intent is truly
ambiguous, ask one focused question rather than inventing project context.

## Inspect Without Starting Review

Establish the local Git target and the intended changes through read-only
inspection. Choose exactly one source: unstaged working changes (`--working`),
staged changes (`--staged`), or committed branch changes against an explicit
reference (`--branch REF`). Do not assume the reference is main or include
untracked files that Git's selected diff does not contain.

If command forms are unknown, use [bootstrap.md](bootstrap.md) and supported
help checks. No separate Atom checkout or inspection of installed Python source
is needed. Missing commands require an installation proposal and consent, not
automatic installation or PATH changes.

Read the root module/configuration only as needed for the selected review.
Missing root `go.mod` does not require `atom init`: disclose that Go tooling will
be skipped. Offer setup separately only if the developer wants it; review intent
is not permission to create a module or repair source.

## Propose Before Probes Or Paid Work

Present one concrete plan, then ask for approval and stop:

- Target directory and exact diff selector/reference.
- Actual reviewer model identifiers, number of runs, concurrency and expected
  submission count. Include availability probes in the call budget: two models
  with one run each can involve two probes plus two review submissions. Do not
  promise a token or monetary ceiling the runtime does not enforce.
- Normal Go checks, missing/skipped evidence and relevant side effects. Go checks
  may invoke project build commands, dependencies, toolchains and caches; ordinary
  review is not inherently offline, read-only or free of cache writes.
- Report format and exact report/audit paths, including any directories created.
- The review-only exit: report and triage, not fixes, setup, phase advancement,
  commit, push or publication.

Recommend one run per model and concurrency 1 as a bounded starting choice,
not a change to CLI defaults. Choose at least two different reviewer models,
neither the authoring model. Resolve unknown identities/authorship explicitly;
do not infer independence from a label. This is skill policy, not CLI enforcement.

Use actual approved identifiers rather than silently accepting CLI defaults.
Repeated `--model NAME` selects reviewers; without it the CLI has built-in
defaults. It does **not** resolve reviewer model roles from `.atom/config.json`.
That file may independently configure Go-version policy. General role advice in
[model-guidance.md](model-guidance.md) does not change this CLI-specific contract.

No reviewer availability probe or review submission occurs before approval.
Earlier setup/phase approval is not automatically approval of this review spend.
If declined, do not launch reviewers, create the bundle or modify the target.
A changed selector, additional runs/models, installation, gate bypass, fix or
publication requires a separately approved scope. Never silently retry a failed
review with more spend or a different toolchain.

## Execute Only The Approved Command

These are alternatives, not a batch to run. Replace MODEL_A and MODEL_B with
approved available identifiers and use the approved branch reference:

```text
atom review --working --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
atom review --staged --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
atom review --branch main --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
```

Add `--json` only when that output was selected. Use the successful command form
from bootstrap. Keep normal gates enabled; do not add `--skip-toolchain`, change
Go versions or repair the diff to get past a failure. Existing explicit advanced
options remain available under their own approved scope, not as automatic recovery.

Formatting checks selected surviving changed Go snapshots without rewriting them.
Build, vet, test and race checks instead examine the working module, not an
isolated staged index or committed branch tree. Passed race tests cover exercised
paths only. Absent optional analyzers and missing-module tooling exclude nothing.

Surface actual required-gate failures and stop this bounded action. An exit-0
report with missing `go.mod` is still unverified tooling evidence, not a verified
build or application. Distinguish skipped checks, unavailable/silent/unparsed
responses, partial participation and genuinely empty findings. No usable response
is not a clean review. If fewer than two qualifying independent models answered,
report that the skill's multi-model obligation remains unmet; do not invent
participation or automatically retry.

## Persist And Triage Without Adopting A Lifecycle

The CLI emits its report to stdout; it does not choose a phase path. The skill
proposes a small standalone bundle, for example:

```text
specs/reviews/<slug>/review.md
specs/reviews/<slug>/findings.md
specs/reviews/<slug>/decisions.md
```

Choose the exact permitted paths with the developer before creating anything.
For phase review, retain `specs/{project}/phase-NN-{slug}/review.md` and the
project's existing findings/decisions locations instead.

Preserve the actual runtime report and participation/evidence limitations.
Always produce `findings.md` and `decisions.md`, even when they say "No findings."
and "No deviations." Use `atom-write-artifact` for these `specs/**` artifacts,
obtaining its repository-scoped permission on first use. Check existing paths;
do not overwrite conflicting work. Any writer refusal or nonzero exit is a
blocker: surface it and stop, without a generic editor or alternate path.

If the developer declines audit-file creation, explain that the skill cannot
complete its persisted audit under this plan. Do not silently drop the records
or force a phase directory. Direct CLI stdout behavior remains available and
unchanged; that is not permission to execute a different paid plan.

Triage high-consequence findings with the developer. Record deferrals/rejections
and reasons. Any fix is a separate approved action with appropriate verification,
not part of review-only consent.

**Standalone stops here:** present report, triage and remaining limitations.
Do not invoke ship, start another phase or modify source automatically.
**Phase review** presents its normal gate and may recommend its next beat; that
recommendation does not authorize executing it.

---
name: review
description: 'Standalone or phase multi-model review of a Go diff, merged into one report with severities. Keywords: review, code review, multi-model review, review my changes, review the diff, critique.'
---

# /atom:review

Reviews a diff with **two or more different models** and merges their findings into one
report.

## Why more than one model

A model reviewing its own output shares its own blind spots. It will not flag the
misunderstanding that produced the code, because it still holds that
misunderstanding.

> **The reviewing model must not be the model that wrote the code.**

This is the entire point of the skill. A single-model self-review is not a substitute,
and running one instead is the rationalization this skill exists to prevent.

## When to use

- For a bounded standalone review, without Atom initialization or phase state
- After `/atom:tdd` for a phase
- Before `/atom:ship`
- Any time a diff is large enough that reading it once isn't enough

## Writing artifacts

Send complete review reports, findings, and decisions as UTF-8 standard input to
`atom-write-artifact <relative-path>`. Treat any refusal or non-zero exit as a blocker;
never bypass it with a generic editor or another shell command.

## Step 0 — Scope, propose and wait

Read [standalone-review.md](../atom/references/standalone-review.md) first.
Follow its mode, prerequisite, consent, model-budget and artifact contract in
both standalone and phase contexts. Explicit review-only intent remains standalone
even in an initialized project. Do not require phase discovery or onboarding.

Propose the exact target/diff, actual models, runs/concurrency, evidence and file
effects before availability probes or review submissions. Wait for approval;
refusal launches no reviewers and creates no bundle. Do not call `atom review`
merely to discover the diff or probe models before that gate.

## Step 1 — Establish the diff without calling reviewers

```bash
git diff main...HEAD             # inspect committed changes against agreed main
git diff --staged                # inspect staged changes
git diff                         # inspect unstaged working changes
```

Choose only the intended source/reference; main above is an example, not a default.
Inspect surrounding code as needed for triage. The CLI supplies the selected diff
and its evidence, not an automatic whole-file context or approved design spec.
Do not claim reviewers received context that was not actually supplied.

## Step 2 — Let the toolchain answer first

No separate command: the gate runs inside `atom review`, before the models.

For a normal review with a root Go module, Atom runs `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, `go test`
and `go test -race`, plus `staticcheck`, `errcheck` and `govulncheck` when they are
installed.

Review formatting checks whole surviving changed Go files from the selected
working-tree, staged or committed-branch snapshot, using stdin without rewriting
source. Untouched files are not scanned. The report names checked paths and
outside-module or nested-module exclusions; zero applicable files means SKIPPED,
not a formatting pass. Other review checks retain their existing module-wide
scope, and standalone `atom check` retains module-wide formatting.
Those module-wide checks run against the working tree, not an isolated staged
or committed tree. Without root `go.mod`, tooling is explicitly skipped: an exit-0
report does not verify a build. Missing optional tools exclude nothing.

**A failing required gate stops the review.** Reviewing code that does not compile, or
that `go vet` already objects to, spends model attention on a question that has an
exact free answer — and the findings would be about code you are about to change
anyway.

What passed is then written into the prompt as **excluded**: the models are told not to
re-report an ignored error, a vet diagnostic, a formatting complaint, or a data race on
a tested path. That exclusion is the mechanism that frees attention for the rest of this
page.

These rules keep the exclusion honest:

- **A tool that did not run excludes nothing.** If `errcheck` is not installed, the
  prompt says so and ignored errors stay in scope. Suppressing a category nobody checked
  is how real bugs go missing.
- **Clean is not absent.** `go test -race` only observes paths the tests actually
  executed. Concurrent code with no test is unchecked, not safe — and the prompt says
  that in those words.
- **Formatting proof is file-scoped.** Only the checked snapshots are excluded
  from formatting review; excluded modules and a skipped formatter are not clean.

`--skip-toolchain` bypasses the gate. The prompt then tells the models that nothing was
checked and nothing is excluded, so a skipped gate costs attention rather than silently
hiding findings.
Do not select this bypass or another Go version as automatic failure recovery;
the shared entry contract requires approval of changed evidence/scope.

### Optional exact Go selection

The launch module's existing `.atom/config.json` may set `review_go_version` to an
exact stable `1.X.Y` patch (X >= 21). `--go-version 1.X.Y` overrides it for one run;
`--go-executable PATH` selects an already installed direct `bin/go` (Windows:
`bin/go.exe`) and requires an effective version. No installation, automatic upgrade,
ancestor lookup or version inference from `go.mod` occurs. Malformed present config
is an explicit error. Explicit paths resolve from launch cwd before PR preparation;
target checkout policy never replaces the frozen launch request.

Bounded installed-location discovery may need an explicit path for custom layouts.
Selected direct Go gates and selected-root gofmt retain existing gate semantics;
pinned Makefile build/test delegation fails before probes or recipes rather than
bypassing the project's build. Unpinned delegation is unchanged. Advisory helper-Go
settings are selected, not analyzer binaries/compiler internals or model tools.
Child-only settings do not change defaults or make dependency activity network-free.

Reports/prompts distinguish requested from observed versions. Configured pins with
`--skip-toolchain`, or requests outside a root Go module, remain `not_run` with no
observed executable/probes. Explicit Go flags plus `--skip-toolchain` are usage
errors. Missing, mismatched or changed executable identities and required failures
still block review; no compiler-text-based continuation is permitted.

## Step 3 — Run the models

```bash
atom review --branch main --model MODEL_A --model MODEL_B --runs 1 --concurrency 1
```

Run only the complete approved command. MODEL_A and MODEL_B are placeholders for
actual approved available models, neither the author. Use the agreed selector;
working/staged alternatives are in the shared reference. Runs=1/concurrency=1 is
a bounded recommendation, not the CLI default.

Each model run receives the full selected diff and evidence, not a separate
invocation for each file. Runs do not receive each other's findings; concurrency
is controlled by the approved option. The CLI uses repeated `--model` values or
built-in defaults, not general model-role resolution from `.atom/config.json`.
Report unavailable, silent, unparsed or insufficient independent responses
honestly; do not substitute a clean review or automatically retry.

## Step 4 — What reviewers look for

Only successful, applicable toolchain evidence is excluded. Unchecked concerns remain
in scope. What is left is
the set of questions no tool can answer — and it is deliberately short, because a
reviewer handed thirty concerns reports on none of them well.

| Priority | Category | Why no tool catches it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Wrong logic** | It compiles, vets clean and the tests pass — because the tests assert the wrong thing |
| 2 | **Untested concurrency** | The race detector only observes paths the tests ran. A goroutine with no test is unchecked |
| 3 | **Misleading names** | A name that says the wrong thing costs every future reader, and no linter can tell |
| 4 | **Code that resists extension** | A wide interface or a package-level dependency forces the next change to edit working code |
| 5 | **Contract drift** | The code disagrees with the approved design spec, which no tool has read |
| 6 | **Tests that cannot fail** | A green suite that asserts nothing looks identical to a green suite that works |
| 7 | **Unvalidated input** | `govulncheck` finds known holes in dependencies, never the one you just wrote |

Severity still comes from consequence. A finding that cannot be stated as "this breaks
when X" is a preference, and preferences are the findings reviewers drop first. That is
measured, not assumed: seeded defects phrased as style preferences were reported by
nobody, while defects with a visible consequence were reported by everybody — even when
the reviewer was handed the exact rule.

[go-style.md](../atom/references/go-style.md) is the reference behind priorities 3 and 4.
Use it to explain a finding, not as a checklist to walk: thirty rules handed to a
reviewer produce worse coverage than seven.

Formatting in the checked file snapshots is **not** reviewed. `gofmt` settled it
for those files only; a skipped formatter or an excluded module proves nothing
about formatting there.

> **Where the real instruction lives.** This table guides *your* triage. The sentences
> actually sent to the models are `REVIEW_PROMPT` and the toolchain block in
> `tools/atom/review.py`. Changing this table alone changes nothing the models see —
> if you want different findings, change the prompt and re-measure.

## Step 5 — Capture the actual merged report

The runtime groups findings by file and line proximity, retaining every message
and severity disagreement. This is not semantic deduplication: nearby reports
may describe different defects. It emits Markdown or JSON to stdout.

Persist the report at the approved mode-specific path from the shared reference.
Standalone uses its small review/findings/decisions bundle; phase review retains
`specs/{project}/phase-NN-{slug}/review.md` and existing project audit locations.

Each merged finding carries:

- **Severity** — critical / high / medium / low, with disagreements retained
- **Agreement** — participating models and per-model reporting runs
- **Location** — `file:line`
- **Messages** — the original findings; a concrete suggested fix is not guaranteed

**Agreement is a signal, not a verdict.** Read critical/high findings individually,
including single-model findings. Group proximity or identical synthetic replies
are not proof of independent corroboration or correctness.

## Step 6 — Triage with the developer

Go through critical/high findings together. For each: propose a separately
approved fix, defer to `findings.md` with a reason, or reject with a reason.
Review-only approval does not authorize editing source.

**Reject freely, silently never.** Reviewers are often wrong about a codebase they saw
in fragments. A rejected finding with a written reason is a good outcome; a finding
quietly dropped is a lost bug.

Every approved code fix requires appropriate verification (`atom check` for
phase Go implementation). Every deferral and rejection is recorded.

## Step 7 — Report

Present the actual report, participation/tooling limits, triage and what remains
open. Always persist findings/decisions, explicitly empty when appropriate.
Standalone stops without fixes, phase advancement or publication. Phase review
presents its existing gate; a next-step recommendation is not permission to act.

---

## Done when

- [ ] Exact scope, model/probe budget and output effects approved before calls
- [ ] Applicable gates passed, or approved missing/skipped evidence is explicit
- [ ] At least two **different** models reviewed, none of them the author of the code
- [ ] Actual supplied context and response/participation limits stated
- [ ] Findings grouped, severity-ranked, with messages/disagreements retained
- [ ] Critical/high findings, including single-model ones, triaged with developer
- [ ] Any separately approved fixes verified; no review-only source edits
- [ ] Review, findings and decisions persisted at approved locations

## Next

Standalone: stop at the review result.

Phase review: after its gate, recommend `/atom:ship` or the next phase's
`/atom:poc` when applicable. Do not execute it automatically.

limits: Preparation only. No agents, probes, test reruns, staging, installations or production edits.
